newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem Steel sees relatively good demand.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem Steel sees relatively good demand.

text.p: Bethlehem Steel Corp said Wednesday demand from the major steel consuming sectors of the economy continues to be relatively good.
"We believe that the U.S. economy will continue on a course of moderate and sustainable growth and low inflation," the company explained.
"Currently, we have a good backlog of orders and are working to implement our previously announced price increases in our short-term markets," Bethlehem Steel said.
Noting General Motors Corp is a major customer, it said it hoped GM would reach a labor settlement soon.

Bethlehem Steel said it is "investing in facilities that will grow our business, and we will continue to divest businesses that do not achieve satisfactory performance or fit with our strategy of concentrating on steel and rebuilding our financial strength."
Wednesday it announced plans to sell four divisions and write down its Coke Division as an impaired asset, saying this will result in a fourth quarter charge of $375 million.
It also announced third quarter earnings before a $15 million restructuring charge of $23 million, or $0.12 per share, down from $34 million, or $0.22 per share, last year.
Bethlehem Steel said third quarter sales slipped to $1.17 billion from $1.22 billion in the year-earlier quarter, as steel shipments slipped to 2.2 million tons from 2.3 million.
It said raw steel production from Basic Steel Operations was also off -- to 2,359,000 tons from 2,565,000 in 1995's September quarter.

The company said directors declared quarterly dividends on its preferred and again omitted payment of a dividend on common. Bethlehem Steel's last common payment was $0.10 a share on December 10, 1991.
Bethlehem Steel said income from operations at its Basic Steel Operations segment declined to $47 million before the restructuring charge in the latest quarter from $68 million a year earlier.

It said the decline was principally due to lower realized prices and lower shipments which were partially offset by an improved mix from a higher percentage of coated and cold-rolled shipments and improved costs at its flat-rolled operations.

During the third quarter, Bethlehem said, its Burns Harbor Division completed its "Big Heat" project that will increase its steelmaking capability by nearly 400,000 tons per year. This additional steelmaking capability will reduce Burns Harbor's need for purchasing higher-cost semi-finished steel.
It also said the construction of the Chicago Cold Rolling Joint Venture is progressing on schedule and is expected to commence operations later this year.
The Steel Related Operations segment's losses from operations marrowed to $7 million from $11 million.

Bethlehem Steel capital expenditures were $206 million for the first nine months of 1996 compared with $205 million during the year-earlier period. Capital expenditures are currently expected to be about $275 million in 1996.

"We contributed $60 million to our pension fund during the third quarter of 1996, for a total of $155 million so far this year. Additional contributions to the pension fund will be made during the fourth quarter 1996, as appropriate," it said.

The company said it repaid $77 million of debt and capital lease obligations during the first nine months of 1996 and expects to repay about $15 million of such obligations during the remainder of the year. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
